title: This Tiny Creature Turns into a Hulk and Eats Its Family!
summary:
Have you ever seen a movie where a normal person turns into a huge, angry monster? That's kind of what happens to a tiny creature called Euplotes gigatrox! This single-celled living thing is so small you need a microscope to see it. Usually, it eats bacteria and other tiny microbes. But sometimes, a few of them grow to more than twice their normal size and start eating their own brothers and sisters!

Scientists discovered this "Hulk" microbe in gunk from an aquarium filter in Curaçao, an island in the Caribbean. The creature looks a bit like an insect with lots of tiny hairs around its mouth. When it turns into a giant, it first gets a big mouth, then starts running around like crazy. Once it catches a smaller sibling, it stuffs it into its mouth and eats it!

The giant form can't swim like the normal ones; it can only walk in circles. But here's the cool part: the giant can shrink back to normal by splitting into smaller cells. A normal cell divides once a day, but a shrinking giant can make up to 16 normal cells in five days! Scientists think studying this weird creature might help us understand how simple life forms evolved into complex ones like us.
why_it_matters: Even a creature you need a microscope to see can behave like a movie monster, and studying it helps scientists understand the story of life from tiny cells to humans.

background_read: Curaçao (a small Caribbean island that is part of the Kingdom of the Netherlands) has warm seas and reefs where many tiny organisms live.
Single-celled life forms were among the earliest forms of life on Earth, long before plants and animals appeared.
Microbes are everywhere — in soil, water, and even inside your body — and most of them are harmless or helpful.
